# Tapanīya Sutta (Iti 30 (It 2.3 PTS It 24))

**ID:** Iti 30 (It 2.3 PTS It 24)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Tapanīya Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Tapanīya Sutta* ("Mortifying", Iti 30) is the third discourse in the second chapter (Dukanipāta) of the *Itivuttaka*. The discourse addresses two states that cause remorse and torment (*dhammā tapanīyā*), arising from the realization of having engaged in misconduct (bodily, verbal, and mental) while failing to cultivate wholesome conduct [Bodhi 2012]. Mrs. Rhys Davids notes that *tapanīya* denotes "burning" states of conscience experienced when reflecting on having done what ought not to have been done and having neglected what ought to have been done [Mrs. Rhys Davids, Buddhism]. The ethical category of *tapanīyā dhammā* versus *atapanīyā dhammā* also constitutes an established dyad in the Abhidhamma *mātika* of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, where *tapanīya* states are formally defined as bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct that burn or torment the mind with remorse [Rhys Davids 1900; Müller 1885; Tan 2015].

 Resembling parallels are found in the *Dhammapada* (Dhp 140), *Gāndhārī Dharmapada* (G-Dhp 201–223), *Udānavarga* (UV 28), and the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 5.174, AN 6.45).

**Sources**

- [Rhys Davids 1900] C. A. F. Rhys Davids, Buddhist Manual of Psychological Ethics (1900) — Exposition of tapaniyā as the flush of heat upon realizing bad deeds.
- [Müller 1885] Edward Müller, Dhammasaṅgaṇī (1885) — Text of the Dhammasaṅgaṇī mātika and definition of tapaniya dhamma.
- [Bodhi 2012] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Numerical Discourses of the Buddha (2012) — Explanation of dhammā tapanīyā as misconduct and failure to do good.
- [Tan 2015] Tan Poh Beng, Survey of the Essence of Dhammasangani in Abhidhamma (2015) — Explanation of the Tapanīyā dyad in the Abhidhamma mātika.
